1. To introduce and impart students to Bioinformatics, its applications and 
understandingofdatabasesofBioinformaticswithdifferencesbetweenvarious databases. 
2. To learn and demonstrate the data storage, retrieval from different resources and 
sequence, structure visualization. 
3. To illustrate the tools required questions related to genomics and proteomics. 
4. To provide the opportunity to think, apply the tools and methods used in the course eg: to address 
the issues related to structural bioinformatics.

Course Contents: 
Unit 1: --- Introduction and Applications of Bioinformatics 
History, importance, opportunities and challenges of Bioinformatics. Data generation: 
Generation of large-scale molecular biology data. (Through Genome sequencing, 
Protein sequencing, Gel electrophoresis, NMR Spectroscopy, X-Ray Diffraction, 
microarray and Next Generation Sequencing: Data Analysis). Applications of 
Bioinformatics. 
 
 
 
8 Hrs. 
Unit 2: --- Bioinformatics Resources 
NCBI, EBI, ExPASy, RCSB, DDBJ: The knowledge of databases and bioinformatics 
tools available at these resources, organization of databases: data contents, purpose and 
utility. Open access bibliographic resources and literature databases: PubMed, BioMed 
Central, Public Library of Sciences (PloS), CiteXplore. 
 
 
 
7 Hrs. 
Unit 3: ---Introduction to Bioinformatics data and databases 
Types of Biological data: - Genomic DNA, Complementary DNA, Recombinant DNA, 
expressed sequence tags, Sequence- Tagged Sites, Genomic survey sequences; 
Primary/Genomic Databases: - GenBank, EMBL, DDBJ; Composite Databases: -
NRDB, UniProt; Literature Databases: - Open access and open sources, PubMed, 
PLoS, Biomed Central, NAR databases; Bioinformatics Resources: - NCBI, EBI, 
ExPASy, RCSB. 
 
 
 
 
8 Hrs. 
Unit 4: -- Sequence Analysis 
Sequence Analysis: Basic concepts of sequence similarity, identity and homology, 
definitions of homologues, orthologues, paralogues and xenologues Scoring matrices: 
basic concept of a scoring matrix, Matrices for nucleic acid and proteins sequences, 
PAM and BLOSUM series, matrix derivation methods and principles. 
 
 
 
 
6 Hrs. 
Unit 5: --Sequence alignment 
Measurement of sequence similarity; Similarity and homology. Pairwise sequence 
alignment: Basic concepts of sequence alignment, Needleman and Wunsch, Smith and 
Waterman algorithms for pairwise alignments, gap penalties, use of pairwise alignments 
for analysis of Nucleic acid and protein sequences and interpretation of results. 
 
 
 
 
 
8 Hrs. 
Unit 6: ---Introduction to Molecular Structural Bioinformatics 
Introduction to Molecular Modeling and Simulation, QSAR and QSPR; brief 
introduction to protein structure hierarchy. Modeling applications – prediction of 
secondary structure of Protein and RNA. Docking Process – Protein preparation, 
ligand building, setting of boundary box, Prediction of Binding pockets, pocket 
analysis, running of docking calculations. 
 
 
 
 
8 Hrs.

Course Contents:  
Unit 1:-Introduction to Biological Macromolecules  
Decoding Biological Macromolecules,types of double helices A, B, Z and 
their geometrical as well as structural feature, Genome Sequencing,Post 
Genomic Era, RNA secondary and tertiary structures, t-RNA tertiary 
structure 
8 Hrs. 
Unit 2:-Protein:  
Protein Chemistry, Chirality, Peptide bond and Levels of protein structures, 
anatomy of proteins – Hierarchical organization of protein structure – 
Primary. Secondary, Super secondary, Tertiary and Quaternary structure; 
Ramachandran Map. X-ray crystallography, NMR techniques and cryo-
electron microscopy. 
8 Hrs. 
Unit 3:- Gel-based proteomics  
Sample preparation and pre-analytical factors, Sample preparation: Pre-
analytical factors, Sample preparation: Protein extraction and quantification, 
One-dimensional electrophoresis, Introduction to 2-DE 
6 Hrs. 
Unit 4:---Two-dimensional gel electrophoresis (2-DE)  
8 Hrs. 

2-DE: Second dimension, staining & destaining, 2-DE: Gel analysis, 2-DE 
Applications, 2-DE Applications (contd.) & Challenges 
Unit 5:-Basics of mass spectrometry  
Fundamentals of mass spectrometry, Chromatography technologies, Liquid  
chromatography, Mass spectrometry: Ionization sources, Mass spectrometry: 
Mass  
analyzers, MALDI sample preparation and analysis, Hybrid mass 
spectrometry  
configurations   
8Hrs. 
Unit 6:--- Advancement in Proteomics  
Proteomics applications, Challenges in proteomics, OMICS and translational 
research,  
Quantitative proteomics, SILAC: In vivo labelling, iTRAQ: In vitro 
labelling, TMT: In 
vitro labelling, Quantitative proteomics data analysis 
8 Hrs.
